sources.entry: Aseprite - Animated sprite editor & pixel art tool (Windows, macOS, Linux).

summary.one_liner: Aseprite is a paid-license animated sprite and pixel art editor with layers, frames, animation preview, and export to sprite sheets and GIF.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Aseprite as a program for creating animated sprites, with layers and frames as separate concepts. It supports RGBA, Indexed (up to 256 colors) and Grayscale color modes, with color profiles. Animation tools include real-time preview and onion skinning, and animations can be exported or imported as sprite sheets, GIF, PNG sequences, and other formats (FLC, FLI, JPG, BMP, PCX, TGA). Pixel-art tools listed include Pixel Perfect freehand, shading ink, custom brushes, outlines, and tiled mode. The README also mentions Lua scripting, a command line interface for automating tasks, customizable keyboard shortcuts, and undo/redo with non-linear undo.
use_cases: automate sprite exports from the command line
notable: Separate layers and frames model with onion skinning and real-time animation preview
Pixel-art tools such as Pixel Perfect freehand mode, shading ink, and wide pixels
Lua scripting and a CLI for batch automation
Export to sprite sheets, GIF, and PNG sequences
caveats: Source and official binaries fall under an End-User License Agreement (EULA), not an open-source license
Steam releases follow the Steam Subscriber Agreement
Educational licenses are available only to teachers at institutions for in-class use
summary.license: EULA for source code and official binaries (proprietary end-user license; some included modules are MIT); Steam releases under Steam Subscriber Agreement
